source_refs.note: ii) Expansion of solids: a main subheading of 5.11 General properties of solids, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 109-109.

blocks.text: The expansion is the property in which spaces between constituent particles are increased. In case of solids the forces of attractions are so strong that increase of temperature hardly affects their relative positions. The particles in a solid have vibrational motions about their mean positions. Increase in temperature of solids hardly increases their volume. No doubt, there are parameters like coefficient of linear and cubic expansions of various solids, but these are negligible as compared to liquids and gases.
